5      Risk Classification
The risk rating methodology used by Cairo Security Clan follows the principles established by the CVSS risk rating methodology. The
severity of each finding is determined by two factors: Likelihood and Impact.
Likelihood measures how likely an attacker will uncover and exploit the finding. This factor will be one of the following values:
    a) High: The issue is trivial to exploit and has no specific conditions that need to be met;

    b) Medium: The issue is moderately complex and may have some conditions that need to be met;
    c) Low: The issue is very complex and requires very specific conditions to be met.
When defining the likelihood of a finding, other factors are also considered. These can include but are not limited to Motive, opportunity,
exploit accessibility, ease of discovery, and ease of exploit.
Impact is a measure of the damage that may be caused if an attacker exploits the finding. This factor will be one of the following values:
    a) High: The issue can cause significant damage such as loss of funds or the protocol entering an unrecoverable state;
    b) Medium: The issue can cause moderate damage such as impacts that only affect a small group of users or only a particular part
       of the protocol;
    c) Low: The issue can cause little to no damage such as bugs that are easily recoverable or cause unexpected interactions that cause
       minor inconveniences.
When defining the impact of a finding other factors are also considered. These can include but are not limited to Data/state integrity, loss
of availability, financial loss, and reputation damage. After defining the likelihood and impact of an issue, the severity can be determined
according to the table below.

                                                                       Likelihood
                                                       High         Medium           Low
                                            High      Critical       High          Medium
                                  Impact
                                           Medium      High         Medium           Low
                                            Low       Medium         Low      Info/Best Practices

To address issues that do not fit a High/Medium/Low severity, Cairo Security Clan also uses three more finding severities: Informational,
Best Practices and Gas
    a) Informational findings do not pose any risk to the application, but they carry some information that the audit team intends to
       formally pass to the client;
    b) Best Practice findings are used when some piece of code does not conform with smart contract development best practices;
    c) Gas findings are used when some piece of code uses more gas than it should be or have some functions that can be removed to
       save gas.

6       Issues by Severity Levels
6.1      High

6.1.1    Centralized Protocol Architecture
File(s): src/validator_registry/validator_registry.cairo, src/lst/lst.cairo, src/delegator/delegator.cairo
Description: Current architecture creates single points of failure where compromised admin keys or malicious admins could drain user
funds, manipulate staking rewards, or freeze the protocol entirely. A truly decentralized liquid staking protocol would require permissionless
validator participation, immutable core logic, fee caps, timelock mechanisms, and decentralized governance.
Some points of centralization:
    − The add_delegator function in validator_registry.cairo:195-211 grants infinite token approvals to any delegator address added by
      the config manager. This allows admin-controlled delegators to withdraw any unassigned funds without restrictions.
    − Only CONFIG_MANAGER can add/remove validators.
    − Validators can be disabled at any time by admin.

    − Contracts are upgradeable by single address approval.
This centralization represents a critical systemic risk that undermines the protocol’s security model. Users must trust administrators com-
pletely, as no technical safeguards prevent fund misappropriation. The protocol operates more like a custodial service than a decentralized
system.
Recommendation(s): Consider re-design the structure and best effort on decentralization
Status: Acknowledged

Update from the client: The protocol currently maintains centralized control over key functions like validator management and contract
upgrades, but the team is actively working toward decentralization by reducing dependencies on centralized functions and increasing
transparency. Contract ownership is managed through a timelock contract with a 3-day delay, with the timelock itself controlled by a
3-of-4 multisig.

6.2.2    Validator fee has no cap limit
     File(s): src/validator_registry/validator_registry.cairo
     Description: Validator Registry contract settings can be set at the constructor or at the set_settings(...) function. However, the
     set_settings(...) function doesn’t validate that any of those settings are valid. The rewards_fee_bps value can be set to any amount
     at any time.

 1   fn set_settings(ref self: ContractState, settings: ValidatorRegistrySettings) {
 2       // @audit-issue There is no fee cap set
 3       self.common.assert_config_manager();
 4

 5       self.settings.write(settings);
 6   }

     Recommendation(s): Consider adding maximum fee limit check.
     Status: Fixed
     Update from the client: Fixed in e1c0028

content:
6.3.2    Relayer can have unlimited fees from swap
     File(s): src/swap_extensions/swap_extension.cairo
     Description: The swap(...) function can be called only by the relayer. However, the relayer can pass anything as the integrator_-
     fee_amount_bps parameter. There aren’t any checks done in the swap function. Also, we are assuming the relayer can send fees to any
     address, which is an expected behaviour.

     Recommendation(s): Consider adding a constant limit and assert integrator_fee_amount_bps value is lower than or equal to that
     limit.

     Status: Fixed
     Update from the client: Fixed in a004902

content: 6.4     Informational

6.4.1    Slippage check can be improved
File(s): src/swap_extensions/swap_extension.cairo
Description: In the swap(...) function, there are checks token_from_amount > 0 and token_to_min_amount > 0. These checks
are sufficient to ensure that AVNU part slippage checks are properly handled. However, they can be improved by adding a check that
token_to_min_amount = token_to_amount to ensure parameters are properly calculated.
Recommendation(s): Consider adding token_to_min_amount <= token_to_amount assertion.
Status: Fixed
Update from the client: Fixed in 83fd921
